t: This grand building on Marylebone Road is The Landmark London, a five-star hotel. It opened as the Hotel Great Central, built by the Great Central Railway, and it was designed by the architect Sir Robert William Edis. Like many railway hotels, it declined once the motor car took over. In the Second World War it served as a military convalescent home, and later it was the headquarters of the British Railways Board. It reopened as a hotel in 1993, and it's one to admire from the street.
